title: Kth Largest Element
contract: Return the kth largest value including duplicates, with 1 ≤ k ≤ n. Compare repeated maximum extraction with a size-k heap.
brute: boolean[] used=new boolean[a.length];int value=0;for(int t=0;t<k;t++){int best=-1;for(int i=0;i<a.length;i++)if(!used[i]&&(best<0||a[i]>a[best]))best=i;used[best]=true;value=a[best];emit("Select the next largest unused value","rank",t+1,"value",value);}return value;
optimal: PriorityQueue<Integer> heap=new PriorityQueue<>();for(int x:a){heap.add(x);if(heap.size()>k)heap.remove();emit("Keep only the k largest values seen","value",x,"heap",heap);}return heap.element();
reasoning: Repeatedly select an unused maximum; keeping a boolean array handles duplicate values correctly.
A min heap of size k retains the k largest values in the processed prefix.
The heap root is the smallest retained value, hence the kth largest. This is a streaming solution; randomized quickselect can improve expected batch time to linear.
